currentTitleEn: Interpret states of matter and transitions
currentDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann feste, flüssige und gasförmige Zustände anhand beobachtbarer Eigenschaften unterscheiden und Übergänge zwischen ihnen als Zustandsänderungen desselben Stoffes erklären.
currentDescriptionEn: The learner can distinguish solid, liquid and gaseous states by observable properties and explain transitions between them as changes in the state of the same substance.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Feste, flüssige und gasförmige Zustände eines Stoffes unterscheiden sich in beobachtbarer Form und Raumerfüllung. Schmelzen, Erstarren, Sieden, Verdunsten, Kondensieren, Sublimieren und Resublimieren ändern den Zustand, nicht die Identität des Stoffes.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: The solid, liquid and gaseous states of a substance differ in observable shape and the space they occupy. Melting, freezing, boiling, evaporation, condensation, sublimation and deposition change its state, not the identity of the substance.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Anhand vorgelegter Beobachtungen eines Stoffes benennt die lernende Person Ausgangs- und Endzustand sowie den passenden Übergang, unterscheidet Sieden von Verdunsten anhand von Blasenbildung im Flüssigkeitsinneren gegenüber Verdunstung an der Oberfläche und erklärt, weshalb der Stoff derselbe bleibt.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: Given observations of a substance, the learner names the initial and final states and the matching transition, distinguishes boiling by bubbles within the liquid from evaporation at its surface, and explains why it remains the same substance.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Bei einem neuen, beschriebenen Fall, in dem ein anderer reiner Stoff beim Abkühlen unmittelbar von gasförmig zu fest übergeht, erkennt die lernende Person Resublimation statt Kondensation und begründet die erhaltene Stoffidentität.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In a new described case where a different pure substance changes directly from gas to solid on cooling, the learner identifies deposition rather than condensation and explains that the substance retains its identity.

rationale: Keep. The current German and English descriptions are equivalent, accurate and concise: observable state properties and the identity-preserving character of a state change are explicit. The official HE G9 chemistry curriculum, printed p. 11, lists melting, boiling, freezing, condensation, sublimation, deposition and evaporation under states and transitions; the current general wording includes these without turning the description into a list. The separate successor goal addresses particle-model explanations, so the particle illustration does not widen this AB1 goal or serve as learner evidence. No current V2 understanding-evidence profile is supplied; create one to spell out the named transitions, the boiling/evaporation distinction and a direct gas-to-solid transfer. The checked HE row supports this scope; raw all-jurisdiction applicability alone does not verify every effective source projection.
